title: Mechanical and HVAC Safety Boundaries
summary: Distinguish safe thermal learning from industrial HVAC service.
objectives: Classify safe classroom and professional HVAC activities.
Explain why permission and escalation matter.

vocab.def: Authorized and trained for a particular professional task.
Passing a concern to an authorized person or team.

sections.heading: Learn the boundary
sections.body: Diagrams, synthetic telemetry, safe temperature experiments, calculations, and simulations are classroom learning. Refrigerant handling, compressor or pump service, pressurized systems, industrial fan service, electrical HVAC service, and live controls changes belong in qualified professional environments.

sections.heading: Stop and escalate
sections.body: A student should not open an industrial unit or modify building systems. Record observations, protect safety, and escalate when the scenario leaves the classroom.

practice.prompt: A simulated cooling alarm suggests opening a live unit. What is the safe response?
practice.answer: Document the evidence and escalate; do not open or service the unit.

quiz.question: Which activity is safe in this course?

lab.objective: Classify thermal activities by safety boundary.

reflectionPrompt: Why is stopping and escalating a technical skill?
